facts.statement: Ciridops is an extinct genus of Hawaiian honeycreepers that lived on the islands of Hawaii, Molokai, Kauai, and Oahu.
facts.quote: Ciridops is an extinct genus of Hawaiian honeycreeper species that occurred in prehistoric and historic times on the Hawaiian islands of Hawaii, Molokai, Kauai and Oahu.

facts.statement: These birds had a strong bill with an arched culmen where the upper jaw overlapped the lower jaw at the base.
facts.quote: The bill of these birds was strong. The culmen was arched, and the maxilla overlapped the mandible at the base.

facts.statement: The nostrils of these birds were covered by a membrane.
facts.quote: The nostrils were covered by a membrane.

facts.statement: The birds possessed large wings and a moderate tail with pointed feathers.
facts.quote: The wings were large and the tail was moderate with pointed rectrices.

facts.statement: The genus was established in 1892 by Alfred Newton based on the ʻula-ʻai-hawane, originally named Fringilla anna by Sanford B. Dole in 1879.
facts.quote: This genus was created in 1892 by Alfred Newton in an article published by the journal Nature on the basis of the ʻula-ʻai-hawane, which was named Fringilla anna by Sanford B. Dole in 1879.

facts.statement: The ʻula-ʻai-hawane was the only species observed in historic times until it was last seen in 1892.
facts.quote: The ʻula-ʻai-hawane, which was last seen in 1892, is the only species that survived into historic times

facts.statement: The genus belongs to the family Fringillidae and the subfamily Carduelinae.
The genus lived during the Late Pleistocene, between 0.129 and 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Late Pleistocene (0.129 to 0.0117 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the nearest relatives of Ciridops might have been from the genus Loxops.
facts.quote: The nearest relatives might have been from the genus Loxops.

rejected.statement: Three other species are known only from subfossil remains found in late Quaternary deposits.
rejected.quote: three others Ciridops cf. anna from Molokai, Ciridops sp. from Oahu, and the stout-legged finch (Ciridops tenax) from Kauai are only known from subfossil remains found in late quaternary deposits.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'from subfossil remains found in late Quaternary deposits'
